title: Evaluating Negative Sampling Approaches for Neural Topic Models
read_from: arXiv preprint 2503.18167v2 (published version: IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence)
subcategory: negative sampling in VAE topic models
task: Measuring the effect of decoder negative sampling on neural topic models
problem: Negative sampling helps representation learning elsewhere, but its effect on unsupervised topic models was not studied comprehensively.
architecture: Decoder negative sampling with a triplet loss (margin 1) added to seven VAE-based NTMs (CombinedTM, ZeroShotTM, ProdLDA, NeuralLDA, ETM, SCHOLAR, GSM); hyperparameters tuned with OCTIS Bayesian optimisation; compared with contrastive NTMs and an encoder-side variant.
key_results: ProdLDA NPMI on GN rises from 0.056 to 0.144 with negative sampling; CombinedTM from 0.081 to 0.142.
SCHOLAR-Neg gives the best 20NG and Wiki40B NPMI (0.180 and 0.181).
Negative sampling beats the vanilla model for every vocabulary size tested on Wiki40B (1,000-8,000 words).
strengths: Systematic study across seven NTMs, four datasets and eight topic counts; no extra trainable parameters.

limitations.text: Training time increases because negative samples must be computed; no theoretical explanation yet for why decoder-side sampling works better.
Improvements are small or absent for some model-dataset pairs (e.g. M10 CV for CombinedTM 0.466 to 0.462).
